function.name: recall_conversations
function.description: Search every past conversation with the user by a few key words. Returns dated excerpts, newest first.

query.description: a few key words to look for

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Only for things a human must do on your desktop: signing in to a website, or passing a CAPTCHA or bot check. Not for permission or questions: ask those in your normal reply. In a background task this pauses until the user has done it.

message.description: what the user needs to do, written to him as 'you', e.g. 'Please sign in to LinkedIn in the browser on my desktop.'

function.name: notify_user
function.description: Send the user a notification right now (to Updates in their phone and desktop apps). Not for reminders: anything set with schedule_task already arrives there by itself at the right time.

message.description: the notification, written to him as 'you'

function.name: start_background_task
function.description: Start a job that you work on by yourself in the background, so the user doesn't have to wait in the chat. He gets a phone notification with the result.

instructions.description: everything needed to do the job, written as instructions to yourself

title.description: a short name for the job

function.name: schedule_task
function.description: Set a reminder, or schedule a job for later or on repeat. For a reminder ("remind me ..."), give reminder_text: that exact text is sent to the user's phone and desktop apps at that time. For a job (daily check, report), give instructions: you do it in the background when it runs and the user gets the result. Call this whenever the user asks to be reminded.

reminder_text.description: for reminders: the exact message to send, written to the user, e.g. 'Time to stretch.'

instructions.description: for jobs: what to do each time, as instructions to yourself

when.description: copy the user's own words for the time, e.g. 'in 2 minutes', 'tomorrow 08:00', 'weekdays 07:30'. Use e.g. 'daily 08:00', 'weekdays 07:30', 'mondays 09:00', 'every 2 hours', 'hourly', 'in 30 minutes', 'tomorrow 18:00', '2026-12-24 09:00', or a cron expression like '0 8 * * 1-5'.

function.name: list_scheduled
function.description: List the scheduled jobs and when each runs next.

function.name: cancel_scheduled
function.description: Cancel a scheduled job by its number.

function.name: list_tasks
function.description: List recent background tasks and their status/results.

function.name: list_models
function.description: List the AI models you can run on, and which is your main one.

function.name: ask_other_model
function.description: Hand one self-contained job to another installed AI model and get its answer back. You stay on your own model. list_models shows what's installed.

prompt.description: the full job, with everything the other model needs to know

function.name: calendar_events
function.description: The user's calendar: their events for today or the next few days (your own calendar, plus Google Calendar if connected). Your own events have #numbers for calendar_change and calendar_remove.

days.description: how many days ahead, from now (default 1 = today)

function.name: calendar_add
function.description: Put an event in the user's calendar (your own calendar, which you remind them about 15 minutes before). Use for appointments, plans and birthdays; use schedule_task for plain reminders.

when.description: copy the user's words: 'Tuesday 3pm', '25 Dec 14:00', '24/12' (all day), 'tomorrow 18:00', 'every Monday 6pm' (repeats)

duration_minutes.description: how long (default 60, or all day for a date with no time)

function.name: calendar_change
function.description: Move, rename or change the length or place of one of your own calendar events, by its #number from calendar_events.

function.name: calendar_remove
function.description: Delete one of your own calendar events by its #number from calendar_events (a repeating event stops repeating).

function.name: weather
function.description: The weather for the user's home town (set in brain.json): now, today, or the next few days.

function.name: week_recap
function.description: Looking back: what the user asked you about and what you did together over the last 7 days, for summaries and LinkedIn post ideas. Not for what's coming up (that's calendar_events).

function.name: convert_file
function.description: Convert a file the user attached (or one you made) to another format, and get a download link for the result. Images: png, jpg, webp, gif, bmp, tiff, ico, avif, heic (optionally resized). Audio: mp3, wav, ogg, flac, m4a, aac, opus. Video: mp4, webm, mkv, mov, gif, or any audio format to pull out the sound.

file_id.description: the file id shown with the attachment

format.description: the target format, e.g. png, mp3, mp4

width.description: optional new width in pixels (images and video)

height.description: optional new height in pixels (images and video)

quality.description: optional image quality 1-100 (jpg/webp), lower is smaller

function.name: switch_model
function.description: ONLY when the user explicitly asks you to change your main model: switch to it, e.g. 'qwen3:14b'. Downloads it first if needed.

function.name: list_add
function.description: Add things to one of the user's lists (shopping, to-do, or any list they name).

function.name: list_show
function.description: Show a list (numbered), or with no list given, which lists exist.

function.name: list_done
function.description: Tick things off a list, by their numbers from list_show or their names.

function.name: list_clear
function.description: Empty a list completely (only when the user asks).

function.name: note_save
function.description: Save a note for the user (something to look up later, e.g. 'the router password is on the back').

function.name: note_search
function.description: Find the user's notes by a few words (or list the latest with no words).

function.name: note_delete
function.description: Delete a note by its #number.

function.name: deadline_add
function.description: Track a deadline (assignment, form, payment). The user is reminded a week, 2 days, 1 day and 3 hours before.

function.name: deadlines_show
function.description: The user's upcoming deadlines.

function.name: deadline_done
function.description: Mark a deadline as done by its #number.

function.name: card_add
function.description: Add a revision flashcard for the user's studies (anything they're revising). Write clear exam-style questions with short, correct answers.

topic.description: e.g. networking, cryptography, linux, law and ethics

function.name: quiz_next
function.description: Get the next revision card that's due, to ask the user. Ask the question, wait for their answer, then mark it with quiz_mark.

function.name: quiz_mark
function.description: Record whether the user answered a revision card right (it comes back later) or wrong (it comes back soon).

function.name: quiz_progress
function.description: How the user's revision is going, per topic.

function.name: currency_facts
function.description: Convert an amount of money written in words, e.g. '50 dollars in pounds', at today's rate.

text.description: the amount and currencies, in words

function.name: calculate
function.description: Work out arithmetic exactly instead of in your head: + - * / ** ^ brackets and 'N% of M'.

function.name: date_maths
function.description: Exact date sums, never search the web for these. Weekday of a date: start=the date. Days until or between dates: start=today (or the first date), end=the other date. A date plus or minus time: start and add_days or add_months. Dates as YYYY-MM-DD, or today/tomorrow/yesterday.

start.description: the date to start from (default today)

end.description: optional second date, to count the days between

add_days.description: optional days to add (negative to go back)

add_months.description: optional months to add (negative to go back)

function.name: date_facts
function.description: Every date in a piece of text worked out: Christmas, Easter, '14 Feb 2027', 'in 3 weeks', '90 days from today', with its weekday and how many days away it is.

text.description: the words containing the dates, e.g. the user's question

function.name: clock_maths
function.description: Add or take away hours and minutes from a time of day, e.g. when a film ending or a journey arrives.

hours.description: hours to add (negative to take away)

minutes.description: minutes to add (negative to take away)

function.name: convert_units
function.description: Convert a measurement: length, weight, volume, speed, data size, area or temperature.

from_unit.description: e.g. fahrenheit, miles, kg, pints, mph, GB

to_unit.description: e.g. celsius, km, lb, litres, km/h, MiB

function.name: convert_currency
function.description: Convert money between currencies at today's exchange rate.

function.name: send_screenshot
function.description: Take a screenshot of your own desktop and send the picture to the user, so they see it themselves. Use this whenever they want to see your screen; look_at_desktop only lets you see it.

function.name: send_screen_recording
function.description: Record your desktop for a set number of seconds and send the video. You can't act while it records, so to show yourself doing something use start_screen_recording and stop_screen_recording instead.

function.name: start_screen_recording
function.description: Start recording a video of your own desktop, to show the user yourself doing something ("send me a video of you searching for X"). Then do it with your other tools (use_tools unlocks the browser or desktop ones), then call stop_screen_recording, which sends the video. Starting gives you the browser and desktop tools.

function.name: stop_screen_recording
function.description: Stop the recording start_screen_recording began and send the video to the user.

function.name: send_file
function.description: Send the user a picture, video or any other file from your own desktop computer, e.g. something you downloaded or made.

path.description: the file's path on your computer, e.g. ~/Downloads/photo.jpg

function.name: send_picture
function.description: Find a picture on the web and send it to the user ("show me a picture of ..."), or send the picture or video at a web address.

query.description: what the picture should show, e.g. 'red panda'

url.description: or: the web address of a picture or video to send

function.name: make_document
function.description: Make a real file and send it to the user: a Word document, PDF, PowerPoint, Excel spreadsheet, CSV, web page, e-book or text file. Write the whole content yourself first. Only say you've made a file after this returns a link.

title.description: the document's title, also used for the file name

content.description: the full content in Markdown (# headings, lists, **bold**, tables). For pptx, each '# ' or '## ' heading starts a slide. For xlsx or csv, a Markdown table or CSV text

format.description: one of docx, odt, pptx, html, epub, rtf, md, txt, pdf, xlsx, csv
